plate_findings.evidence: Caption: skull AP radiograph with size measured as longest transverse distance between the ends of each coronal suture (yellow arrows); visual: open infant coronal sutures/anterior fontanelle region.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real infant ultrasound from the disease-focused article on deformational plagiocephaly; panel shows the captioned anterior fontanelle measurement with white arrows/calipers. No vocabulary key covers fontanelle size, so it is recorded as a proposed finding rather than invented as an allowed finding. B: Real AP skull radiograph from infants with deformational plagiocephaly in the disease-focused article; yellow arrows mark the coronal suture ends used to measure the anterior fontanelle, and the sutures appear patent/non-fused as expected in positional rather than synostotic deformity.
panels.attribution_text: Lee et al. Ultrasonographic Measurement of Anterior Fontanelle Size in Infants with Deformational Plagiocephaly.. Journal of clinical medicine 2024. doi:10.3390/jcm13175012. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Measurement of anterior fontanelle size using ultrasonography (a) and an anterior–posterior (AP) radiograph of the skull (b). (a) The size of the anterior fontanelle was defined as the longest transverse distance between the skull bones, as indicated by the white arrows in the ultrasound image; (b) similarly, in the skull AP radiograph, the size was determined by the longest transverse distance between the ends of each coronal suture, marked by the yellow arrows.
in_text_mentions: ing of both lambdoid sutures was performed, and a short cine loop of the flattest portions of the occipital bone was recorded. We also analyzed the correlation between the CVA and anterior fontanelle size. Anterior fontanelle size was defined as the longest transverse distance between the skull bones at the frontal head on ultrasonography and as the longest transverse length on AP radiographs of the skull, according to a previous study (Figure 2) [26]. Ultrasonographic assessments were performed by the same researcher (KDR); two measurements were obtained to verify the intra-rater reliability.

plate_findings.evidence: Skull AP radiograph showing open anterior fontanelle and patent cranial sutures; caption: 'Radiographs of skull in anteroposterior (A) and lateral (B) views... Size of anterior fontanelle (SAF) = T + L/2'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Genuine patient skull AP radiograph from an infant with positional plagiocephaly (article on helmet therapy outcomes). The image shows the open anterior fontanelle and patent cranial sutures, a recognized radiographic finding in positional plagiocephaly used to differentiate it from craniosynostosis. Yellow caliper line marks the transverse diameter (T) of the anterior fontanelle. B: Genuine patient skull lateral radiograph from an infant with positional plagiocephaly (article on helmet therapy outcomes). The image shows the open anterior fontanelle and patent cranial sutures, a recognized radiographic finding in positional plagiocephaly used to differentiate it from craniosynostosis. Yellow caliper line marks the longitudinal diameter (L) of the anterior fontanelle.

in_text_mentions: the reduction rate as the monthly decrease in the diagonal difference before and after correction, divided by the correction period. The growth rate was defined as the monthly increase in the difference in head circumference before and after correction. The size of anterior fontanelle was measured with the skull anteroposterior (AP) and lateral view x-ray. Transverse diameter(T) of anterior fontanelle was measured in the AP view, and the longitudinal diameter(L) was measured in the lateral view. The average of the two diameters was defined as size of anterior fontanelle (SAF) [26] (Figure 3).

Caption: 'asymmetry in the occipital region with notable flattening on one side'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: 3D CT reconstruction of an infant skull with occipital flattening/asymmetry explicitly captioned as characteristic of positional plagiocephaly; real patient imaging of the configured target disease. B: Second reconstruction rendering from the same pre-treatment infant skull study; caption applies to the whole figure and describes unilateral occipital flattening typical of positional plagiocephaly.
